beats.intro: Chapter fifty. [[sub]]Multiplying and dividing monomials uses the power rules you just learned, one base at a time.
beats.parts: A monomial is a number times some powers of variables. [[ex]]Three x squared y [[expand]]means three, times x times x, times y. [[coef]]The number in front is the coefficient. [[bases]]Each variable is its own base.
beats.mult: Multiply four x cubed y by five x squared y to the fourth. [[sort]]Since you can multiply in any order, sort the factors by kind: [[lanes]]numbers together, x's together, y's together. [[nums]]Multiply the numbers: four times five is twenty. [[xs]]For x, add the exponents: three plus two is five. [[ys]]For y, one plus four is five. [[ans]]The product is twenty x to the fifth y to the fifth.
beats.div: Dividing works the same way. [[ex]]Twenty-one x to the sixth y to the tenth, divided by seven x to the fourth y cubed. [[frac]]Write it as a fraction, and split it by kind. [[nums]]Twenty-one divided by seven is three. [[xs]]For x, subtract: six minus four is two. [[ys]]For y, ten minus three is seven. [[ans]]The quotient is three x squared y to the seventh.
beats.negdiv: Sometimes the bottom has the bigger exponent. [[ex]]Three a to the fifth divided by ten a to the ninth. [[nums]]Three tenths can't be simplified. [[xs]]For a, five minus nine is negative four. [[pos]]To write it with a positive exponent, a to the negative four moves to the bottom as a to the fourth. [[ans]]So the result is three over ten a to the fourth.
beats.power: Now a power raised to a power. [[ex]]x cubed, squared, [[copies]]means two copies of x cubed multiplied together. [[expand]]Each copy is three x's, so there are two times three, six x's. [[ans]]x cubed, squared, is x to the sixth. [[rule]]To raise a power to a power, multiply the exponents.
beats.powmono: When a whole monomial is raised to a power, the power goes to every factor inside. [[ex]]Three a to the seventh b to the fourth, all squared. [[arrows]]The outside two reaches the three, the a to the seventh, and the b to the fourth. [[each]]Three squared is nine, a to the seven times two is a to the fourteenth, and b to the four times two is b to the eighth. [[ans]]The result is nine a to the fourteenth b to the eighth. [[warn]]A common slip is to forget the coefficient and write three a to the fourteenth b to the eighth.
beats.combo: Put it all together. [[ex]]Five a cubed b to the fourth, squared, times two a to the fifth b, cubed. [[pow]]First, raise each monomial to its power: twenty-five a to the sixth b to the eighth, and eight a to the fifteenth b cubed. [[mult]]Then multiply: twenty-five times eight is two hundred, a to the six plus fifteen, and b to the eight plus three. [[ans]]Two hundred a to the twenty-first b to the eleventh.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]To multiply monomials, multiply the coefficients and add the exponents of each base. [[w2]]To divide, divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents. [[w3]]To raise a power to a power, multiply the exponents, and apply the power to every factor, coefficient included. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter fifty, multiplying and dividing monomials.
